slices.brief:
We are building Twinclue for the Codex x TwitchCon Hackathon. Read SPEC.md and AGENTS.md in this repository first and follow AGENTS.md strictly.

Slice 1, the game core, with no Twitch and no model yet:
1. Set up the project: package.json (type module, scripts: dev, build, start, test, typecheck), tsconfig with strict mode, vitest, fastify, ws, zod, dotenv. Install the dependencies.
2. src/puzzle/types.ts: a Puzzle type (id, category, difficulty, answer, aliases, halfA, halfB) and a zod schema for it.
3. src/puzzle/validate.ts: checks that a puzzle is fair: neither half contains the answer or any alias (case and accent insensitive, also as a substring of a longer word), both halves are non-empty and under 160 characters, the answer is short (at most 4 words), and no blocklisted word appears. Return a list of reasons when it fails.
4. src/puzzle/pack.ts: a built-in pack of at least 40 hand-written, genuinely good split puzzles across categories (general, games, music, science, sport, food, geography, movies). Each half must be ambiguous on its own and the two halves together must point to exactly one answer, like the Paris example in SPEC.md. Every puzzle in the pack must pass validate.
5. src/game/referee.ts: normalise a guess (case, accents, punctuation, articles like "the"), accept the answer or an alias, and accept small typos with an edit distance threshold that scales with answer length. Return accepted, rejected, or unclear (close but not within the threshold).
6. src/game/round.ts: a Round state machine for two communities A and B: start, guess(community, user, text, at), timeout, and the rule that the round is won only when at least one viewer from each community has a correct guess. Track the first solver on each side, guesses per side, and the time to solve. Limit each viewer to one guess every 3 seconds.
7. src/game/session.ts: a session with a sequence of rounds, scoreboard, streak, and save/load to data/session.json.
8. Tests for all of the above, including: every pack puzzle validates, the referee typo rules, a round that is solved by only one community is not won, rate limiting, and session persistence.

Run npm test and npm run typecheck until both pass. Then write a short summary of what you built and any decisions in DECISIONS.md, and commit nothing (I will review and commit).

slices.brief:
Review of slice 1 (I committed it). Good work, but the puzzle pack breaks the core idea of the game. In many puzzles one half alone gives the answer away, for example "Its formula is H2O" (Water), "Its recurring hero is named Link" (Zelda), "Her fans are known as Swifties", "Chihiro works in a bathhouse", "Riders compete for the yellow jersey". Each half on its own must fit at least two well-known answers; only the two halves together may point to exactly one.

Slice 2a, fix the puzzles:
1. Add two fields to Puzzle: halfAAlsoFits and halfBAlsoFits, each a list of at least two other well-known answers that the half alone also fits (and that the other half rules out). Validate: both lists have at least 2 entries, neither contains the answer or an alias, and each entry is ruled out by the other half (this last part is a written promise, just check the lists are present and distinct).
2. Rewrite the whole pack to 60 puzzles that really work this way, with useful aliases (for example "Pac-Man": "pacman"). Keep them fun, family friendly and recognisable worldwide; include some India-friendly ones (cricket, Bollywood, Indian food and places) since one of our test communities is Indian. Mix difficulty (easy, medium, hard) honestly.
3. The reveal on stream will show the also-fits lists ("Your half alone could have been Tokyo or Rome"), so make them interesting.
4. Add tests: every puzzle validates, ids are unique, no answer appears in either half, both also-fits lists have 2 or more entries.

Slice 2b, Twitch integration behind interfaces (I will provide real credentials later; build and test with fakes now):
1. src/twitch/auth.ts: OAuth authorization code flow for the bot account and for each broadcaster, served by Fastify at /auth/start?role=bot|a|b and /auth/callback; scopes: bot needs user:read:chat user:write:chat user:bot; broadcasters need channel:bot and channel:read:redemptions. Store tokens in data/tokens.json (gitignored), refresh them automatically before expiry.
2. src/twitch/eventsub.ts: an EventSub WebSocket client (wss://eventsub.wss.twitch.tv/ws) that handles welcome, keepalive, reconnect and revocation messages, and creates subscriptions through Helix: channel.chat.message for both channels (condition broadcaster_user_id + user_id of the bot), channel.shared_chat.begin, update and end, and channel.channel_points_custom_reward_redemption.add. Parse chat messages into { channel: 'a'|'b', user, text, sourceChannel } using source_broadcaster_user_id when present, so it works in Shared Chat too.
3. src/twitch/chat.ts: send chat messages with POST https://api.twitch.tv/helix/chat/messages, with a small queue that respects rate limits.
4. src/app/commands.ts: chat commands: "!g <answer>" to guess, "!tc start", "!tc skip", "!tc score" (start and skip only for the broadcaster or moderators, using badges from the chat event).
5. Wire it into src/server.ts with config from .env (TWITCH_CLIENT_ID, TWITCH_CLIENT_SECRET, PUBLIC_URL, CHANNEL_A, CHANNEL_B) and an .env.example.
6. Tests with a fake EventSub socket and fake Helix: message parsing including shared chat, command permissions, reconnect handling, and token refresh.

Keep npm test and npm run typecheck green. Update DECISIONS.md. Do not commit.

1. Work in rounds: rewrite or replace every failing puzzle, re-audit only the changed ones, and repeat until all 60 pass, keeping the earlier passes untouched. Stop after 8 rounds at most; if some still fail, replace them with new puzzles rather than weakening the referee.
2. What fails is predictable: a half that names a unique attribute (a famous lyric, a named character, a record, a nickname, a defining shape) gives the answer away. Good halves describe a category plus a property shared with several well-known things; the other half adds a second property that intersects to one answer. The hourglass and lighthouse puzzles are good models.

Only the win celebration and the reveal may grow, for at most 8 seconds, then shrink back.

## Part 1. The blind audit was too lenient. Fix it before anything else.

I read all 28 generated puzzles. Many give the answer away in a single half, and some are false:
- gen-042 half A: "Indian cricketer known as the 'Master Blaster' who debuted at age 16" (the audit solver said Kapil Dev).
- gen-160 half B: "Located on the banks of the Yamuna River in Agra" (solver said Mehtab Bagh).
- gen-016 half B: "featured on the Indian 10-rupee note" (solver said Nehru).
- Also clear giveaways: gen-036 Lagaan A, gen-104 Dangal A and B, gen-379 Kilimanjaro A, gen-283 Beethoven A, gen-133 Jai Ho A, gen-421 Mumbai B, gen-251 Miso A.
- False or invented facts: gen-001 Mysore Palace B (no such 1995 film scene), gen-004 Pav Bhaji B (nonsense film link), gen-142 Biryani B (the Land of Five Rivers is Punjab; biryani does not originate there).

Root cause, which I verified by hand: the audit client runs with reasoningEffort 'none' and maxCompletionTokens 128. With reasoning on, both openai/gpt-oss-20b and qwen/qwen3.8-27b name Sachin Tendulkar, Taj Mahal, Mahatma Gandhi and Mysore Palace from those single halves straight away. There is also no check that a clue is true.

Build audit v2:
1. **Solver panel.** `AUDIT_MODELS` in `.env` is a comma list, default `openai/gpt-oss-20b,qwen/qwen3.8-27b`. Use reasoning on (medium, or the model's default if 'medium' is not accepted) and enough completion tokens for reasoning plus JSON (at least 2048). Keep the same blind prompt shape: best answer plus two alternatives.
2. **Pass rule.**
   - A single half fails if ANY solver's best answer is accepted by the referee. The answer appearing among the alternatives is fine and expected; that is the designed ambiguity.
   - Both halves together must be accepted by a majority of solvers.
3. **Fact check.** Run a separate verifier call with `FACT_MODEL`, default `openai/gpt-oss-20b` with reasoning. It is given the answer and each half and returns, for each half, `true`, `false` or `unsure`, plus a short reason. Anything except `true` for both halves fails. Store the reasons in the report.
4. **Batching, to fit free quotas.** One blind request may carry up to `AUDIT_BATCH` clues (default 8), returned as an array keyed by an opaque clue id.
   - A request must never contain two prompts from the same puzzle (half A, half B or both).
   - Write a test that proves this for any pack.
   - Fact checks can batch freely, since they are not blind.
5. **Quota handling.**
   - On a per-minute limit, wait the time Groq names in "try again in Xs".
   - On a per-day limit (TPD or RPD), checkpoint and exit cleanly with a message saying where it will resume. Never lose a finished result.
   - Record per-model token usage in the report.
6. **Report.** The report records audit version 2, the solver models, the fact model, the pass rule and every solver's answers.
   - The fingerprint must include the audit version and models, so v1 results are never reused as v2.

Then:
- Re-audit all 60 current puzzles under v2. Drop every failure.
- Refill with the generator, gated by validation plus audit v2.

Generator prompt changes:
- Each half alone must fit at least three well-known answers.
- Avoid nicknames, unique records, named landmarks, exact dates, award wins and anything that identifies the answer by itself.
- Only well-known, easily verified facts.
- The answer must be something a general Twitch audience knows.

Pack mix:
- Most viewers and the judges are global, so at most 15 India-friendly puzzles (at least 8).
- A strong games category, since this is Twitch.
- The rest spread over general, music, science, food, places and film.
- Use `LLM_MODEL` for generation and fall back to openai/gpt-oss-20b when its daily quota is spent.

Target and tests:
- Target 60 puzzles. If quota runs out before 60, stop cleanly with what passes (the run can resume tomorrow) and tell me the count.
- The tests must assert that every puzzle in the pack has a v2 pass with a matching fingerprint and that the pack has at least 40 puzzles. Do not hard-code 60.

Rewrite `docs/PUZZLE_AUDIT.md` honestly:
- what v1 did;
- the giveaways it let through (use the examples above);
- what v2 changed;
- v2 results per round;
- generation stats;
- the per-puzzle table.

The write-up will say we caught our own audit being too easy on itself, so be exact.

## Part 2. Overlays that teach the game and are fun to watch

I watched the demo at 1920x1080. The look is good. Fix these:
1. **Status pill.** During a live round it says "NEXT ROUND SOON". It must reflect the real state (live round, solved, time up, idle). Fix "1 wins" pluralisation everywhere.
2. **No call to action.** While a round is live, show a clear line: "Type !g and your answer in chat", using the real command prefix from config.
3. **The core hook is invisible.** Show that the other community holds the other half, for example "Community B has the other half. Get your streamer to swap clues." Keep it short and human.
4. **The meter is unlabelled.** Replace it with a clear two-side status:
   - each side shows "Solved by @name" with a check, or "Still searching";
   - plus that side's guess count this round;
   - the round is won when both light up, and the celebration should feel like the two halves snapping together.
5. **Timer.** Larger, with "seconds left" text for screen readers, and urgency styling in the last 10 seconds.
6. **Guess ticker.**
   - Show the last three guesses from this side's chat, sanitised and length-limited, fading out.
   - A correct guess must NEVER show its text on either overlay before the round ends; show "@name got it" instead.
   - Viewers of both streams can see both overlays, so this matters.
7. **Panel preview.** The DEMO badge overlaps the category label.
8. Keep reduced-motion support and the teal/coral identity.

Make the demo exercise all of it: ticker, a masked correct guess, both sides lighting up, a timeout with the urgency style.

Keep the tests, typecheck and build green, and add tests for the ticker masking and the batching rule. Follow AGENTS.md: no em dashes or arrows in user-facing text. Log decisions in DECISIONS.md. When finished, report: the v2 pass count for the old 60, the final pack count, the generation stats, the token usage per model, and anything left for tomorrow's quota.

slices.brief:
Slice 5b: the Puzzle Forge and community lock-in voting. I committed your slice 5 as 6e33861. Do not commit this slice; I review and commit.

## Why
The 8 puzzles audited under v2 all failed, and I confirmed why with my own probes. Free-text clues written by a model point at the most famous member of a set: "a timing aid used during a board game" is answered "hourglass" from one half. A stricter audit cannot fix that; the puzzles have to be built differently.

I ran a small experiment with three solvers: gemini-3.5-flash, gemini-2.5-flash and gpt-oss-20b.
- **Works:** "A country whose flag uses only red and white" plus "A South American country with a Pacific coastline". Single halves got Canada, Switzerland, China, Chile, Chile and Peru. Both halves got Peru.
- **Fails:** puzzles whose answer is the prototype of a set. "An island country in Asia" plus a red-and-white flag gives Japan from half A alone. "More than 100 known moons" gives Saturn.

There is also a scale problem. In a big chat, hundreds of viewers will brute-force any set of 15 candidates within seconds, whatever the per-user rate limit. So the round mechanic has to change too.

## Part 1. Community lock-in voting (replaces "first correct guess per side")
- **Votes.** Each viewer's latest `!g` guess is their one vote in their community. Changing your guess moves your vote.
- **Buckets.** Normalise votes through the referee into answer buckets, so close spellings and aliases of the same answer pool together. Use the puzzle answer and aliases as one canonical bucket and normalised text for the rest.
- **Win rule.** When the timer ends, each community's answer is its plurality bucket. The round is won only if both communities' top answers are correct.
- **Early finish.** If, after at least 15 seconds, both sides' leading bucket is correct and has at least 50 percent of that side's votes, hold it for 5 seconds, then finish.
- **Streamer control.** Streamers can lock early from the panel or with `!tc lock` (mods and broadcasters only).
- **Overlay.** Show the live top three buckets for this side as vote bars with counts, plus the total voters. Never indicate which bucket is correct until the reveal.
  - Remove the per-guess "got it" masking from slice 5. Text is fine to show because correctness is hidden.
  - Sanitise and cap the text, and run it through the blocklist.
  - Show a leading bucket as "Leading: X". This is what makes it fun to watch: chat converging.
- **Reveal.** Show each side's final top answer, whether it was right, "your half alone fitted N answers, including X, Y and Z", the voter counts, and the time.
- **Tiny chats.** One viewer's single vote decides that side.
- **Data structures.** Map of user to bucket plus bucket counts, updated in O(1) per vote. No unbounded history: keep only bounded recent samples for the panel and recap.
- **Referee bug.** `judgeGuess` accepts a guess if ANY word of it is within edit distance, so "is it peru or chile" is accepted. In voting, a vote is the whole normalised guess.
  - Accept exact matches and aliases, plus whole-guess fuzzy matches with the current thresholds.
  - Strip only leading filler such as "is it", "maybe" and "i think".
  - Add tests.
- **Hints.** Keep the `!hint` vote design from the slice 6 notes if you have started it, otherwise leave it for slice 6.

## Part 2. The Puzzle Forge
Puzzles are constructed from curated fact tables by a small constraint search, then audited.

1. **Fact tables** in `facts/<category>.json`. Each entity has a name, aliases, fame (1 to 3, how well a general audience knows it) and typed attributes. Each table has a header stating its sources and licence.
   - Categories and minimum sizes:
     - countries: about 80 well-known ones; attributes are continent, landlocked, coastline oceans, neighbour count and notable neighbours, flag colours, flag features (stripes, cross, star, emblem), driving side, official languages, population band, area band;
     - video game characters: at least 70; publisher, debut decade, species or type, signature colour, silent protagonist, wields a sword, has a sibling in the series, platform of origin;
     - animals: at least 60; class, native continents, diet, pattern, can fly, swims, nocturnal, size band;
     - space objects: at least 25;
     - musical instruments: at least 30; family, played with bow, keys, reed, strings count;
     - foods and dishes: at least 50; origin country, main ingredient, eaten hot or cold, sweet or savoury, served as;
     - sports: at least 30; team or individual, ball or not, players per side, Olympic, played on ice, grass or court.
   - Include India-friendly entities naturally, for example cricket, Indian dishes and Indian animals, and keep the pack global.
   - Use well-known, checkable facts only. Where an attribute is genuinely debatable, leave it out.
2. **Constraint search.** A half is one or two attribute predicates. Find pairs (half A, half B) over one table where:
   - set A has at least 5 members;
   - set B has at least 5 members;
   - A intersect B is exactly the answer;
   - the answer is not the most famous member of either set: at least two members of each set have fame greater than or equal to the answer's.
   This is deterministic, explainable and cheap. Generate many candidates and rank them by set sizes and fame balance.
3. **Phrasing.** Each predicate has a template that produces natural, playful English. The model may polish wording only through a strict prompt: keep every constraint, add no facts.
   - Store the predicates with the puzzle.
   - Re-check the polished text with the fact model: does each half state exactly these predicates?
4. **Fact check.** The facts come from the table, so table errors are the remaining risk. Fact-check each (entity, attribute) used by a kept puzzle once with the fact model, batched, and cache the verdicts. A wrong fact gets fixed in the table, not just dropped.
5. **Audit v2.1**, the same blind machinery, with:
   - Solvers `AUDIT_MODELS=gemini:gemini-3.5-flash,gemini:gemini-2.5-flash,groq:openai/gpt-oss-20b`. Support provider prefixes. Gemini uses its OpenAI-compatible endpoint `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/` with `GEMINI_API_KEY` from `.env` (already set). gpt-oss-20b uses reasoning low.
   - A single half fails if a majority of solvers name the answer as their best answer.
   - Both halves must be answered correctly by a majority.
   - Report and publish the aggregate single-half hit rate and both-halves hit rate across all solvers. That pair of numbers is our headline fairness metric.
   - Handle Gemini free-tier limits (429 with retry info, daily caps) with the same checkpoint and resume behaviour.
6. **Reveal data.** `alsoFitsA` and `alsoFitsB` come from the sets, ordered by fame, so "your half alone could have been" is always true.
7. **Custom packs.** A streamer can drop a CSV in `facts/custom/` (columns: name, aliases, fame, then any attributes) and run `npm run forge -- --table custom/mycommunity.csv`. Document it in the README. This is the "local city" and "community lore" story.
8. **Commands.**
   - `npm run forge` builds candidates, polishes, fact-checks, audits and writes the pack with progress checkpoints.
   - Target 80 kept puzzles across all categories, games well represented, at most 15 India-flavoured. If quota stops it, stop cleanly and report the count.
   - The old pack is retired: keep the files in `docs/archive/` for the write-up, and the game uses only forged puzzles.
9. **Docs.** Update `docs/PUZZLE_AUDIT.md`:
   - v1 (lenient), v2 (strict; free-text puzzles failed, with examples), v2.1 forge results;
   - the headline hit rates;
   - per-category counts and the per-puzzle table with set sizes.
   Be exact; this becomes part of the story.

## Tests
- The constraint search guarantees uniqueness and set sizes, with property tests over random tables.
- Templates never leak the answer or its aliases.
- Vote bucketing, plurality, early finish and the lock command.
- The referee whole-guess rule.
- The committed pack all passes v2.1 with matching fingerprints, and has at least 40 puzzles.

Keep the typecheck and build green. Follow AGENTS.md (no em dashes or arrows in user-facing text) and log decisions in DECISIONS.md. Update the demo so it shows votes converging on both sides and a reveal. When finished, report the forge stats, the hit rates, the pack count, per-model token use and anything left for quota.

I read `data/forge-progress.json`. The machinery is right, but the 80 selected candidates are not shippable:

1. **Duplicates.** Aloy appears 6 times, Kratos 4, Türkiye 4, Link 3, mostly the same predicates with halves swapped.
   - Selection must keep one puzzle per answer and never a swapped mirror.
   - Enforce category quotas for an 80-puzzle target: games 18, geography 14, animals 12, food 12, music 8, space 8, sports 8.
   - Spread fame levels and difficulty.
2. **Wrong facts.**
   - "Chun-Li ... Sony-published": Chun-Li is Capcom. Find how a Sony predicate reached her: a table error or a predicate bug. Add a test that every puzzle's halves are true of its answer according to the table.
   - Link is Hylian, not human. Kratos is a god or demigod. Waluigi's species is debatable. Use speciesOrType values a fan would accept, or drop that attribute where it is contested.
   - Run the planned fact check now: every (entity, attribute) pair used by a kept puzzle goes once to the fact model (Gemini or gpt-oss-20b, batched, cached in `facts/verdicts.json`). Disputed facts are corrected in the table or removed, never silently kept.
3. **Wording.** "human, Sony-published" is not something a streamer wants on screen. Write per-attribute templates in natural, slightly playful English, a full sentence of at most 14 words. Examples:
   - "A hero from a series Sony publishes."
   - "This character first showed up in the 2010s."
   - "Its flag uses only red and white."
   - "A country with no coastline at all."
   Then:
   - two-predicate halves join with "and" grammatically;
   - polishing by the model is optional and must keep exactly the predicates, checked by the existing re-check;
   - no answer, alias or franchise name may leak; extend the leak test to series and franchise names, so "Zelda" in a Link clue counts as a leak.
4. **Audit throughput.**
   - Gemini free tier allows few requests per minute: pace each provider to its limit, with configurable RPM per provider.
   - Respect `retryDelay` in Gemini 429 bodies.
   - Keep auditing while any solver is available, instead of stopping on the first 429.
   - Checkpoint after every batch.
5. **Live pack meanwhile.** Until the audited pack reaches 40, the game uses the audited puzzles plus a clearly labelled "unaudited" fallback in demo mode only. Real mode refuses unaudited puzzles. The tests reflect that.

Run `npm run forge` to completion within the free quotas if possible; it is fine if it takes a while. Report:
- the number of forged candidates;
- deduped picks per category;
- fact-check corrections made;
- the audit pass rate with single-half and both-halves hit rates;
- the final pack size;
- token use.

Keep tests, typecheck and build green. Follow AGENTS.md: no em dashes or arrows in user-facing text.
